correctness.rationale: As a universal guarantee, the iff is correct. A frame on r states with one neighborhood equal to the whole state set for every agent forces at least r completions of any fixed action. For sufficiency, choose a largest copy coordinate k. With x_k fixed the mixed-modulus map is a product of translations; with x_i fixed for i≠k, one can prescribe the target residue modulo m_i by choosing x_k, then uniquely set the other residues by choosing their own labels. This proves slice surjectivity even when some m_i=1. Compose with a surjection onto the actual outcome set. For a prescribed outcome in a fixed action's neighborhood, each other agent can select a neighborhood containing that outcome by the common-union condition and choose copy labels to force it; the nonempty-intersection fallback never creates an outcome outside the fixed neighborhood. The inequality is not asserted to be necessary for each particular easier frame. The supplied checks/verify_budget.py was found and inspected, not executed; its reported finite checks are not the universal proof.
